name: elementary OS 8.1 ARM64 for Surface Pro 11 — v23 live test image
body:
# elementary OS 8.1 ARM64 live image for Surface Pro 11 — v23

Experimental community image prepared with Lexr from the checksum-verified elementary OS 8.1 ARM64 source. This publishes the **exact ISO tested on Surface Pro 11 X1E/OLED on 2026-09-06**, without rebuilding it after the successful test. It is a test prerelease, not an official elementary release.

## What was tested

The maintainer confirmed that the default **X1E/OLED** GRUB entry displayed the elementary logo and spinner, then reached the desktop and language/try/install chooser. Wi-Fi connected and the browser loaded a website. System Information displayed kernel `7.2.0-jg-0sp11v23-qcom-x1e`. The first start took longer than expected; allow time after the spinner. No specific boot duration has been measured.

Lexr creation and independent structural validation passed all 11 checks. The ISO was written using the changed, natively built Lexr on the Surface, with full SHA-256 read-back verification and ejection.

**Not yet qualified:** an actual OS installation, installed custom-kernel/DTB boot, recovery, audio/microphone, pen/touch setup, suspend or other peripherals. X1P/LCD and other Snapdragon devices remain unqualified. Opening the installer chooser is not an installation test. Keep another bootable recovery device and back up your data before considering installation. Disable Secure Boot for this unsigned custom kernel.

## What is included

- The v23 kernel, matching modules and separate X1E/OLED and X1P/LCD device trees. The declared installed profile is X1E/OLED.
- Separate live and installed initramfs images, with the early Surface platform, panel and QRTR dependencies checked against the kernel bundle. Normal desktop boot keeps graphics enabled; separate text and firmware-display diagnostics are available in GRUB.
- Wi-Fi board data prepared from elementary's existing WCN7850 firmware database before the first driver probe.
- Two checksum-pinned public Qualcomm GPU firmware files, with their upstream licence, notices and provenance.
- Linux ARM64 Lexr `v0.4.0-rc.1-6-g927d00e`, its corresponding source, catalogues and licences, and the portable IPTSD `sp11-iptsd-v2` bundle for explicit setup.
- `LEXR_GETTING_STARTED.txt` in the live user's Desktop folder. Open it through Files for bundled-Lexr, Wi-Fi, IPTSD and post-install audio commands. Companion files are retained in the installation payload at `/usr/share/lexr/elementary-media/sp11/companion`; this is structurally checked, not installed-boot qualification.

No private device firmware, Windows captures, SSH keys, ngrok configuration or personal debug helpers are included. Full audio requires the separate permitted same-device firmware/userspace workflow; do that after installation because restarting the DSP can disconnect USB storage supporting the live root.

## Download, verify and write with Lexr

Use Linux or macOS with `curl`, GitHub CLI (`gh`), `zstd` and `shasum`. Image validation and the pre-write check also need Docker with a running daemon, Linux ARM64 container support and at least 24 GiB free workspace; keep additional space for the download and reconstructed ISO. The temporary source-build option below needs Git and Go 1.26 or newer.

Run the checksum-verifying installer as your regular user. Add its user installation directory to the current shell so the newly installed Lexr is available immediately:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/refs/heads/main/install.sh | sh -s

export PATH="${LEXR_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}:$PATH"
LEXR="$(command -v lexr)"
"$LEXR" version

WORK="$(mktemp -d "$HOME/lexr-elementary.XXXXXX")"
cd "$WORK"
```

**Until the elementary PR is included in a stable Lexr release, run this next block too.** At publication, latest stable `v0.3.0` and prerelease `v0.4.0-rc.1` both predate elementary support and cannot validate or write this image. Build the exact tested implementation below; all subsequent commands use its absolute path. Once a stable release containing the elementary adapter is available, the installer above is sufficient and this fallback can be skipped.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh.git lexr-source
git -C lexr-source checkout --detach 927d00e1f672bc177593c6dde1862cb348cce60b
(cd lexr-source && go run ./cmd/lexr-build)
LEXR="$PWD/lexr-source/bin/lexr"
"$LEXR" version
```

Download the complete release, check every published member, and ask Lexr to validate the closed asset set and reconstructed ISO identity:

```bash
TAG=sp11-elementary-os-8.1-v23-20260906
gh release download "$TAG" --repo ooaklee/linux-surface-pro-11-oe --dir image-assets
(cd image-assets && shasum -a256 -c SHA256SUMS)
"$LEXR" image release validate image-assets

ISO=lexr-elementary-sp11-v23-927d00e.iso
cat "image-assets/$ISO".zst.part-* | zstd --decompress --stdout > "$ISO"
printf '%s  %s\n' \
  '82f9b71c610a05c9b42b34e72cc36c121fe549841a55a22b7e3f808c25022884' \
  "$ISO" | shasum -a256 -c -
"$LEXR" image validate "$ISO"
"$LEXR" image devices
```

Keep the reconstructed ISO outside `image-assets`; that directory must contain only the exact published members. Stop if any checksum or validation fails.

Choose the **whole USB device** shown by `image devices`. The actual write erases its contents. Replace the placeholder only after checking the device's size and identity; do not choose your internal system disk. Review the dry run, then perform the write in an interactive terminal:

```bash
DEVICE="<reviewed-whole-USB-device>"
"$LEXR" image write "$ISO" --device "$DEVICE" --dry-run
sudo "$LEXR" image write "$ISO" --device "$DEVICE"
```

Lexr requests an exact device/image confirmation and verifies the complete written length by reading it back. Wait for the final successful receipt and ejection before reconnecting the USB and booting the first X1E/OLED entry. Installing a newer Lexr on the build host does not update the older Lexr already embedded in this ISO; its bundled version remains the tested `927d00e` build.

## Image identity and source

- ISO: `lexr-elementary-sp11-v23-927d00e.iso`, **3,713,728,512 bytes**.
- ISO SHA-256: `82f9b71c610a05c9b42b34e72cc36c121fe549841a55a22b7e3f808c25022884`.
- Builder and embedded Lexr: [927d00e1f672bc177593c6dde1862cb348cce60b](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/commit/927d00e1f672bc177593c6dde1862cb348cce60b). Documentation and catalogue-evidence revision: [7af5a0e36367c36e22843a43ccd962a00be5607d](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/commit/7af5a0e36367c36e22843a43ccd962a00be5607d). These later prose edits do not change the tested ISO bytes.
- Upstream ISO: [elementaryos-8.1-stable-arm64.20260219.iso](https://dl.sda1.eu/linux/elementary/elementaryos-8.1-stable-arm64.20260219.iso), 3,191,691,264 bytes, SHA-256 `85116d48c406ae7cd60c936050a099d4b8610321273f6f0a694796db4d4e86ba`, checked against the [publisher's installation guide](https://elementary.io/docs/installation).
- Kernel packages, corresponding source and terms: [SP11 v23 kernel release](https://github.com/ooaklee/linux-surface-pro-11-oe/releases/tag/sp11-qcom-x1e-7.2.0-jg-0sp11v23).
- IPTSD binaries and corresponding source: [sp11-iptsd-v2](https://github.com/ooaklee/linux-surface-pro-11-oe/releases/tag/sp11-iptsd-v2).
- GPU firmware and notices: [Linux firmware revision 599764611a8ac213c6aa6dad17c941c2f46b53cb](https://gitlab.com/kernel-firmware/linux-firmware/-/tree/599764611a8ac213c6aa6dad17c941c2f46b53cb), retained under `/cdrom/sp11/firmware` and `/usr/share/lexr/firmware`.
- OE release tag anchor: `aba8c0b65ea73422c8e15868606bb934780a066e`, the existing v23 support-source commit; the Lexr builder revision above identifies the remaster implementation.

The assets were produced with `lexr image release prepare` and checked with `lexr image release validate`. `SHA256SUMS`, `image-release-manifest.json`, the image manifest and generated `RELEASE-NOTES.md` describe the closed set and both ordered zstd parts. The private creation journal is not published. All six uploaded assets have also been downloaded afresh from OE: their checksums and closed release set passed validation, the reconstructed ISO matched the exact tested hash and size, and all 11 adapter checks passed using the documented pinned-source Lexr build.

Implementation: [Lexr PR #51](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/pull/51). Remaining qualification: [Lexr issue #49](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/issues/49). Related tested image: [Ubuntu Concept 26.04 v23](https://github.com/ooaklee/linux-surface-pro-11-oe/releases/tag/sp11-ubuntu-concept-26.04-v23-20260905). Report results with the exact image hash, kernel, device variant and tested features; omit credentials and private device captures.
